claims.text: The guide comes from about a year of using Claude every day, written for the people joining the team.
claims.quote: It comes from about a year of doing this every day.

claims.text: Keep sessions separate: every major or recurring topic gets its own Claude session, sometimes its own tab or window, and no thread mixes topics.
claims.quote: Every major topic, and every topic that comes back regularly, gets its own session.

claims.text: A thread is the model's frame of reference; put three projects in one and the model mixes them, doing exactly what it was asked with everything in front of it.
claims.quote: Put three projects in one thread and the model starts to mix them

claims.text: Name every session as project, a pipe, and what is being worked on; agent sessions get an @ in front of the role.
claims.quote: A session you cannot find is a session you will recreate, badly.

claims.text: An agent is a Claude session with a particular focus: a few documents explaining the project, a role.md, and a session named for the role that reads them first.
claims.quote: An agent is a Claude session with a particular focus.

claims.text: The memory of a session is what it has read: its frame of reference and its whole universe for the project.
claims.quote: The memory of a session is what it has read

claims.text: The owner's memory is a collection of websites, graphs and vaults wired together: this site and its llms.txt, the behaviour policy, coding, NFR, Wardley maps and graphs sites, and the vaults behind them.
claims.quote: It is a collection of websites, graphs, vaults, references and materials, wired together

claims.text: The more time spent curating and maintaining those files, the more relevant and accurate the agents are.
claims.quote: The more time I spend curating and maintaining those files, the more relevant and accurate the agents are.

claims.text: When the owner finds a mistake he can usually trace it to a brief that needed to be better or a file that was missing or wrong, and fixes it there.
claims.quote: I can usually trace it back to a brief that needed to be better, or a file that was missing or wrong

claims.text: The review stops being a sign-off and becomes a QA step on the whole setup.
claims.quote: The review stops being a sign-off and becomes a QA step on the whole setup

claims.text: Ask Claude to check what it is not sure of against a source rather than relying on what it learned in training.
claims.quote: do not let it rely only on what it learned in training, ask it to check against a source

claims.text: The idea is access by default, not public by default: inside a company most content can be available to most people, which gives agents most of the benefit.
claims.quote: The idea underneath is access by default, not public by default.

claims.text: Almost everything the owner does is published, mainly for efficiency: nothing needs to be sent, attached or explained twice.
claims.quote: Nothing needs to be sent, attached or explained twice.

claims.text: Vaults are how information moves between agents and people: because a vault is easy to edit it becomes a communication platform.
claims.quote: Because a vault is easy to edit, it becomes a communication platform

claims.text: To share a vault with an agent the owner hands over the vault key, and soon a key pair, not broad permissions; read-only access is a read key.
claims.quote: I hand over the vault key, and soon a public and private key pair, not broad permissions on an account or a drive

claims.text: Four starter prompts, used in some form all the time: starting a project session, starting an agent session, handing over a vault, and ending a session.
claims.quote: Four prompts I use, in some form, all the time.

claims.text: Ask for documents and read the rendered preview; ask for a small proof of concept, because a page you can click is the fastest way to test an idea.
claims.quote: A page you can click is often the fastest way to find out whether an idea holds.

claims.text: Use skills with care: they are loaded into the agent's context and permissions, so read them before turning them on and prefer ones you or your team wrote.
claims.quote: Read them before you turn them on, and prefer ones you or your team wrote.

claims.text: Write the Agent Behaviour Policy before adding a connector, because every connector makes Claude more useful and more dangerous by extending what the session can reach.
claims.quote: Every connector makes Claude more useful and more dangerous, because it extends what the session can reach.

claims.text: With the policies in place the owner is comfortable connecting Claude to much more than he was.
claims.quote: With the policies in place I am now comfortable connecting Claude to much more than I was.

claims.text: For the more agentic workflows, one Cowork session per agent at work, each with its own name, role and policy.
claims.quote: For the more agentic workflows I create a separate Cowork session for each agent.

claims.text: Projects in Claude and ChatGPT are fine, but the owner moved past them because this workflow makes him pay attention to the memory directly.
claims.quote: I find this workflow better because it makes me pay attention to the memory directly

claims.text: Where to start: close the long mixed thread today, write one role.md this week, make the memory findable with an llms.txt, share through a vault, write the policy before every connector.
claims.quote: Open one session per topic and name it "project | work".

claims.text: The statement that chat and Cowork have come together in Claude is the author's observation of the product he uses, not checked against a product announcement.
claims.quote: not a claim checked against a product announcement

claims.text: The prompts are examples to adapt, not a specification.
claims.quote: The prompts are examples to adapt, not a specification.

claims.text: The guide was drafted from a voice memo by agent@riskmandate.ai on 9 October 2026; it works with ChatGPT too, since the tools differ and the habits do not.
claims.quote: It works with ChatGPT too; the tools differ, the habits do not.
